∎

Corollary 3.6
.

Suppose
{c_{*}}=2
. After deleting the nodes
i_{1}
and
i_{3}
from the Dynkin diagram associated to
G
, the component containing
i_{2}
corresponds to a Lie group
\tilde{G}
for which
i_{2}
is a minuscule index.

Proof.

This is a corollary of the proof of the previous lemma. We tabulate below all situations in which
{c_{*}}=2
.

\begin{array}[]{c||c|c|c|c|c|c|c}\mathrm{type}(G)&k&{i_{*}}&i_{1}&i_{2}&i_{3}&\mathrm{type}(\tilde{G})&\tilde{i_{2}}\\
\hline\cr&&&&&&&\\
\hline\cr B_{n}&n&{i_{*}}\neq n&n-{i_{*}}&n&{i_{*}}&B_{\min({i_{*}},n-{i_{*}})}&\min({i_{*}},n-{i_{*}})\\
\hline\cr C_{n}&1&{i_{*}}\neq 1&{i_{*}}&{i_{*}}-1&{i_{*}}&A_{{i_{*}}-1}&{i_{*}}-1\\
\hline\cr D_{n}&1&{i_{*}}\notin\{1,n-1,n\}&{i_{*}}&{i_{*}}-1&{i_{*}}&A_{{i_{*}}-1}&{i_{*}}-1\\
&n&{i_{*}}\notin\{1,n-1,n\}&n-{i_{*}}&n-1&{i_{*}}&D_{\min({i_{*}},n-{i_{*}})}&n-1\\
\hline\cr E_{6}&6&2&5&6&2&A_{1}&1\\
&&3&3&2&5&A_{2}&2\\
&&5&2&1&3&A_{1}&1\\
\hline\cr E_{7}&7&1&6&7&1&A_{1}&1\\
&&2&2&1&2&A_{6}&1\\
&&6&1&7&6&A_{1}&1\end{array}

Note that type
A
has no such simple roots.
∎

Now, although we have described the actions of
w_{0,i_{j}}
on
{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}}
, we have seen that only a certain subword of its reduced expression acts non-trivially. Of course, this subword is exactly a minimal coset representative of
w_{0,i_{j}}
with respect to
W_{i_{j-1}}
; we will denote these subwords with
u_{i_{j}}
. Hence, we obtain the characterization

u_{i_{j}}\in W_{j}\text{ is an element of minimal length such that }w_{0,i_{j}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}})=u_{i_{j}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}}).

(3.15)

We further define
w_{i_{j}}=u_{i_{j}}\dots u_{i_{1}}
for
j\in[c_{*}]
, and we will now show that these
w_{i_{j}}
are minimal coset representatives for
W/W_{P}
by investigating the actions of
u_{i_{j}}
on
{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}
.

Proposition 3.7
.

For
j\in\{1,\ldots,{c_{*}}\}
, we have

\displaystyle w_{i_{j}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=u_{i_{j}}u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})

\displaystyle=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}},

(3.16)

and that each
w_{i_{j}}=u_{i_{j}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
is a minimal coset representative for
W/W_{P}
. Furthermore, for each
j\in[{c_{*}}+1]
, we have

\displaystyle u_{i_{j}}u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}(u_{i_{0}}{\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})

\displaystyle=-({c_{*}}-j+1){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+({c_{*}}-j){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}

(3.17)

with each simple reflection
s_{i}
of
u_{i_{j}}
acting by subtracting
({c_{*}}-j+1)\alpha^{\vee}_{i}
in the action of
u_{i_{j}}
on
u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})
.

Proof.

We prove (
3.16
) as well as the fact that
u_{i_{j}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
is a minimal coset representative of
W/W_{P}
by induction on
j
, combining Lemma
3.5
with the observation that
u_{i_{j}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}})={\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}
. For
j=1
, both statements follow from (
3.10
) combined with
i_{0}=k
and the definition of
u_{i_{j}}
in (
3.15
).

So now suppose that (
3.16
) holds for some
j-1\in\{1,\ldots,{c_{*}}-1\}
, then (
3.11
) holds for
j
and we find that

\displaystyle u_{i_{j}}\bigl(u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})\bigr)

\displaystyle=u_{i_{j}}\bigl(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}}\bigr)=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+u_{i_{j}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}{-1}}})

\displaystyle=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+2{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}.

Furthermore,
u_{i_{j}}
acts only on
-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}
and not on
{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}
. Since
u_{i_{j}}
represents the minimal such action by definition, each action is nontrivial, so
u_{i_{j}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
is a minimal coset representative of
W/W_{P}
. Hence, (
3.16
) holds and
u_{i_{j}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
is a minimal coset representative of
W/W_{P}
for all
j\in\{1,\ldots,{c_{*}}\}
.

To conclude equation (
3.17
) from this, we note that
{i_{*}}=i_{-1}
so that (
3.9
) implies
u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}}+{c_{*}}{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}
. Hence (
3.16
) yields

u_{i_{1}}u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})=u_{i_{1}}(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}}+{c_{*}}{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}}+{c_{*}}\,u_{i_{1}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})\overset{(\ast)}{=\!=}-{c_{*}}{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{2}}}+({c_{*}}-1){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}},

which is (
3.17
) for
j=1
. Note that
u_{i_{1}}
only acted on the minuscule weight
{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}
in equality
(\ast)
, and hence each simple reflection
s_{i}
in a reduced expression of
u_{i_{1}}
acts by subtracting
\alpha^{\vee}_{i}
since
u_{i_{1}}
is the minimal coset representative; the scalar factor
{c_{*}}
now gives the final statement for
j=1
.

For
j\in\{2,\ldots,{c_{*}}+1\}
, (
3.17
) and the final statement follow inductively:

\displaystyle u_{i_{j}}u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})

\displaystyle=u_{i_{j}}\bigl(-({c_{*}}-j+2){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+({c_{*}}-j+1){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}}\bigr)

\displaystyle=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+({c_{*}}-j+1)\,u_{i_{j}}(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j-1}}})

\displaystyle=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+({c_{*}}-j+1)\,u_{i_{j}}u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})

(†)

\displaystyle=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}}+({c_{*}}-j+1)\,(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}})

\displaystyle=-({c_{*}}-j+1){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j+1}}}+({c_{*}}-j){\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{j}}},

which is equation (
3.17
). Again, note that
u_{i_{j}}
only acted on an element in the Weyl orbit of the minuscule weight
{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}
in (
{\dagger}
), and hence we obtain the final statement.
∎

Corollary 3.8
.

We have
u_{i_{{c_{*}}}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{\sigma_{0}({i_{*}})}}
and
u_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{\sigma_{0}(k)}}
. In particular, we have
w^{P}=u_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
.

Proof.

For the first equation, we note that substituting
j={c_{*}}
into equation (
3.17
) gives
u_{i_{{c_{*}}}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}}
. The statement now follows from the fact that
i_{{c_{*}}+1}=\sigma_{0}({i_{*}})
, which one can verify directly from the proof of Lemma
3.5
. The second equation follows directly from combining (
3.16
) for
j={c_{*}}
with (
3.12
). We conclude from this directly that
w^{P}=u_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
, since both sides are minimal coset representatives that map
{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}
to
-{\varpi^{\vee}_{\sigma_{0}(k)}}=w_{0}({\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})
.
∎

Since each
w_{i_{j}}=u_{i_{j}}\dots u_{i_{1}}
is a minimal coset representative, we may define
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
to be the order ideal corresponding to
w_{i_{j}}
. Note in particular that
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
for
j\in[{c_{*}}+1]
, where we define
\mathsf{w}_{i_{0}}=\varnothing
. With this construction, we associate to each
u_{i_{j}}
for
j\geq 1
the subset
\mathsf{u}_{i_{j}}=\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}}\subset\mathsf{w}^{P}
. From the previous proposition, we see that the order ideals
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
allow an easy combinatorial description:

Corollary 3.9
.

The order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
for
j\in[{c_{*}}+1]
is the maximal ideal obtained by adding all possible
\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}
with
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\neq s_{i_{j}}
to
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}}
, where
\mathsf{w}_{i_{0}}=\varnothing
.

Recall that we have illustrated this description already in Section
1
. We now have all the information we need to calculate
\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
as in equation (
3.5
).

Theorem 3.10
.

Let the minimal coset representative
w_{i_{j}}=u_{i_{j}}\dots u_{i_{1}}
be defined as above with corresponding order ideals
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
. Then we have

\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}

where
a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}=\prod_{\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}a_{\mathsf{b}}
, cf. (
2.10
).

Proof.

Recall from equation (
3.5
) that the toric expression for
\phi_{{i_{*}}}
on
U^{\circ}_{-}
is given by

\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}(u_{-})=(-1)^{h}(-a)_{\mathrm{wt}^{-1}(\mathbb{N})}^{\mathrm{wt}},

where
\mathrm{wt}:\mathsf{w}^{P}\to\{0\}\cup\mathbb{N}
is defined as

\mathrm{wt}(\mathsf{b})=\langle\!\langle\Pi(\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b}))\,w_{P}\cdot{\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle,

and where
\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b})
is the order ideal generated by
\mathsf{b}
,
\Pi(\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b}))\in W^{P}
is the minimal coset representative corresponding to
\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b})
(cf. Remark
2.15
), and
\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})
is the index of the simple reflection corresponding to
\mathsf{b}
(i.e.
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})=s_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}
). Note that
\mathrm{wt}(\mathsf{b})
in fact equals the number of copies of the simple root
\alpha^{\vee}_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}
the simple reflection
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})=s_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}
corresponding to
\mathsf{b}
subtracts from
\Pi(\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b})\setminus\mathsf{b})\,w_{P}\cdot{\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}}
.

We have shown in Corollary
3.8
that
w^{P}=u_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}\cdots u_{i_{1}}
, so that the extremal path following
\bar{w}^{P}
from the weight vector of weight

w_{P}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})=u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})

to the lowest weight vector follows the successive actions of the
u_{i_{j}}
for
j\in[{c_{*}}]
. Moreover, in Proposition
3.7
we showed that for each
j\in[{c_{*}}+1]
, each simple reflection
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})=s_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}
corresponding to
\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{u}_{i_{j}}
acts by subtracting
{c_{*}}-j+1
copies of the simple root
\alpha^{\vee}_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}
in the action of
u_{i_{j}}
on the weight
u_{i_{j-1}}\cdots u_{i_{0}}({\varpi^{\vee}_{{i_{*}}}})
. Hence, we find that

\mathrm{wt}(\mathsf{b})={c_{*}}-j+1\quad\text{for}\quad\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{u}_{i_{j}}=\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}},

so in particular we have that
\mathrm{wt}^{-1}(\mathbb{N})=\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
and the toric monomial in equation (
3
) can therefore be expanded as

\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}(u_{-})=(-1)^{h}\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\prod_{\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{u}_{i_{j}}}(-a_{\mathsf{b}})^{{c_{*}}-j+1}.

Since we are in the special case where the weight on
\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
itself is defined by membership in its subideals
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
, we can rewrite this using ordinary order ideals as

\displaystyle\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}(u_{-})

\displaystyle=(-1)^{h}\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\left(\prod_{\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}}}(-a_{\mathsf{b}})^{{c_{*}}-j+1}\right)=(-1)^{h}\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\left(\prod_{\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{j-1}}}(-a_{\mathsf{b}})\right)^{{c_{*}}-j+1}

\displaystyle=(-1)^{h}\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\prod_{m=1}^{j}\left(\prod_{\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{m}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{m-1}}}(-a_{\mathsf{b}})\right)=(-1)^{h+\sum_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\ell(\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}})}\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}.

Now, it turns out that the minus signs cancel, see Remark
3.11
, so we conclude

\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\prod_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}},

as claimed.
∎

Remark 3.11
.

We recall that
\mathrm{wt}(\mathsf{b})
is exactly the number of simple roots the simple reflection
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})
removed from the weight
\Pi(\mathsf{I}(\mathsf{b})\setminus\mathsf{b})
for
all

\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}
, including
\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{u}_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}
since these act trivially. We conclude that we must have removed exactly the height
h
simple roots as defined in (
2.7
) in total, since we have acted with all simple reflections in
\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}=\mathsf{w}^{P}
(cf. Corollary
3.8
). Hence, we conclude that

h=\sum_{j=1}^{{c_{*}}}\ell(\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}})

This is exactly what we claimed in Section
2.2.3
and Remark
2.22
.

For notational convenience, we will define
p_{i_{j}}=p_{w_{i_{j}}}=p_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}
to be the Plücker coordinate with weight
w_{i_{j}}(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=\Pi(\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}})(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})
corresponding to the minimal coset representative
w_{i_{j}}
or equivalently to the order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
. The following Plücker monomials will play an important role in the next section where we compute the polynomials
\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}
corresponding to the
\phi_{{i_{*}}}
.

Corollary 3.12
.

The toric monomial for
\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
found in Theorem
3.10
is contained in the toric expression for
(p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}\dots p_{i_{{c_{*}}}})|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
.

Proof.

By definition, the toric expression of
p_{i_{j}}
contains toric monomials corresponding to all possible embeddings in
\mathsf{w}^{P}
of the order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
corresponding to
w_{i_{j}}
. In particular the identity embedding
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}:\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
is a valid embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}
whose corresponding toric monomial is
a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}}
. Thus, the toric monomial in Theorem
3.10
is contained in the toric expression for
(p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}\dots p_{i_{{c_{*}}}})|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
.
∎

4.
Plücker coordinate denominators from the generalized minors

As we found in Corollary
3.12
, the toric monomial of Proposition
3.10
is contained in the toric expression for the Plücker monomial
p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}\cdots p_{i_{c_{*}}}
, where we denote by
p_{i_{j}}
the Plücker coordinate corresponding to the order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
or equivalently to
w_{i_{j}}\in W^{P}
as defined Section
3
. However, this Plücker monomial in general also contains extraneous terms in its toric expression, and we will now show how to use the combinatorics of order ideals of
\mathsf{w}^{P}
to cancel these out and obtain a Plücker coordinate expression, which we denote by
\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}
, for
\phi_{{i_{*}}}
on
\mathbb{X}^{\vee}
. We start by proving the following simplifying result:

Lemma 4.1
.

The restriction
p_{i_{{c_{*}}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
is a monomial in the coordinates of
U^{\circ}_{-}
.

Proof.

As discussed in Section
2.3.3
, we may compute the restriction of
p_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
to
U^{\circ}_{-}
by finding all possible embeddings of the order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
corresponding to
w_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
into
\mathsf{w}^{P}
. By Proposition
3.7
, the weight corresponding to
\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
,
\Pi(\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}})(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})=w_{i_{{c_{*}}}}(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})={\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}}-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}}
, is join-irreducible (considered in the Bruhat order) since it covers exactly one element (corresponding to the action of
s_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}
). Hence
\mathsf{w}_{{c_{*}}}
has a unique maximal element
\mathsf{b}
and this element has label
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})=s_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}
. Therefore, any embedding
\tau_{{c_{*}}}:\mathsf{w}_{{c_{*}}}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
must have
\tau(\mathsf{b})
as its maximal element. However, by construction
\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{{c_{*}}}}
has no element with label
s_{i_{{c_{*}}+1}}
. Thus, the only embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{{c_{*}}}
is the identity embedding, corresponding to the monomial
a_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}
.
∎

As an immediate consequence, we now obtain the following corollary.

Corollary 4.2
.

If
{c_{*}}=1
, then
\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=p_{i_{c_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
.

Proof.

By Corollary
3.12
, the toric expression for
p_{i_{1}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
contains the desired toric monomial
\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
, and the expression contains exactly one toric monomial by Lemma
4.1
.
∎

On the other hand, we will see that for
{c_{*}}>1
, the
\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}
are never monomials. Instead, we will construct a signed sum of Plücker monomials that cancels all extraneous toric terms. To organize the cancellation, we develop a classification of the toric terms in the restriction of a Plücker monomial. For now, we only consider the case
{c_{*}}=2
; the remaining cases
{c_{*}}\in\{3,4\}
only occur in four cases—
{c_{*}}=3
for
{i_{*}}=4
in
E_{6}
and
{i_{*}}=3,5
in
E_{7}
and
{c_{*}}=4
for
{i_{*}}=4
in
E_{7}
. Rather than handling these four cases in the generality of this section, we will instead apply our construction directly in Appendix
A
.

Definition 4.3
.

For any pair
\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
of order ideals, we say that a filter (upward closed set)
\mathsf{B}\subset\mathsf{w}_{1}
can be moved to
\mathsf{w}_{2}
if there exists a subposet
\mathsf{B}^{\prime}\subset\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
isomorphic to
\mathsf{B}
by a label-preserving isomorphism such that
\mathsf{w}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{B}^{\prime}
is an order ideal. We then define

M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\{\mathsf{B}\subset\mathsf{w}_{1}~|~\text{$\mathsf{B}$ is a minimal (w.r.t.~inclusion) movable filter of $\mathsf{w}_{1}$}\}.

For each
\mathsf{B}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
which can be moved to
\mathsf{w}_{2}
, we will use
\mathsf{B}^{\prime}
to denote the corresponding label-isomorphic subset of
\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
.

Note that the elements of
M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
need not have the same size; minimality only ensures that no strict subsets of an element of
M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
are also in
M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
themselves.

Example 4.4
.

\mathrm{LG}(5,10)=D_{5}^{\mathrm{sc}}/P_{5}
so that

w^{P}=(s_{5})(s_{3}s_{4}s_{5})(s_{3}s_{4}s_{5})(s_{2}s_{3}s_{4}s_{5})(s_{1}s_{2}s_{3}s_{4}s_{5})\quad\text{and}\quad\mathsf{w}^{P}=\raisebox{-14.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright then the elements

height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt},\raisebox{-3.5pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt},\raisebox{-14.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\right)~~\text{resp.}~~\left(\raisebox{6.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt},\raisebox{-14.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\right),

giving an alternative description of
M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
as the set of all minimal filters
\mathsf{B}
(i.e. subsets containing all elements larger than the elements contained) of
\mathsf{w}_{1}
that can be added to
\mathsf{w}_{2}
resulting in a new order ideal.

\lozenge

In order to study the combinatorics of these moves, we define a poset
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
as follows.

Definition 4.5
.

The elements of
\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
will be the set of all pairs of order ideals
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
that can be obtained from the pair
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
by any sequence of moves going from
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
to
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
. More precisely,
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
consists of those pairs
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
such that there exists a sequence of
d\geq 0
moves

\mathsf{B}_{1}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}},\quad\mathsf{B}_{2}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{B}_{1},w_{i_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{1}^{\prime}},\quad\mathsf{B}_{3}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\setminus(\mathsf{B}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{2}),\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup(\mathsf{B}_{1}^{\prime}\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{2}^{\prime})},\quad\dots

with
\mathsf{w}_{1}=\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\setminus(\mathsf{B}_{1}\sqcup\dots\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{d})
and
\mathsf{w}_{2}=\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup(\mathsf{B}_{1}^{\prime}\sqcup\dots\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{d}^{\prime})
, where each
\mathsf{B}_{j}^{\prime}
is the corresponding label-isomorphic subset of
\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus(\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup(\mathsf{B}_{1}^{\prime}\sqcup\dots\sqcup\mathsf{B}_{j-1}^{\prime}))
to the move
\mathsf{B}_{j}
. We define a partial order on
\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
by
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})>(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
if
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
can be obtained from
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
by a sequence of moves starting from
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
. In particular,
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
will be the unique top element of
\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
.

For the rest of this section we will only want to consider moves between elements of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, so we restrict to these
admissible
moves as follows.

Definition 4.6
.

For any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, we call
\mathsf{B}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
is
admissible
if
(\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{B},\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{B}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
and we denote the subset of admissible moves by
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\subset M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. Analogously, we say that
\mathsf{B}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
is
admissible
if
(\mathsf{w}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{B}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{2}\setminus\mathsf{B})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
and we again the subset of admissible moves by
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\subset M_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
.

Note by definition that for any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, we have
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
since
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
is constructed using every
\mathsf{B}\in M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. Moreover, by Remark
2.15
, we can associate to every cover relation in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
a Weyl group element, namely
\Pi(\mathsf{B})\in W
where
\mathsf{B}
is the movable poset. However, note that
M_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
may contain
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
as a proper subset for
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. Furthermore,
\mathsf{B}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
if and only if
\mathsf{B}^{\prime}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{B}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{B}}
, so by construction of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
we have
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\neq\varnothing
for any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
unequal to the top element
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
. In addition, we have a further simplification when studying only the admissible moves.

Remark 4.7
.

Let
L^{\vee}
denote the Levi subgroup of
G^{\vee}
corresponding to the component of the Dynkin diagram of
G^{\vee}
which contains
i_{2}
after deleting the nodes
i_{1}
and
i_{3}
. Then we note that the poset
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
can be identified with the Bruhat order on the weight space of the fundamental representation of
L^{\vee}
corresponding to the node
i_{2}
. In particular, Corollary
3.6
implies that this is a minuscule representation so each cover relation
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
corresponds to an admissible move in
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
of size
1
. Thus for the remainder of this section we will assume that all admissible moves have size
1
.

Using this simplification, we can more easily study the possible moves of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. First, we saw in Example
4.4
that the Weyl group elements
s_{5}
and
s_{2}s_{3}
corresponding to the two moves of
M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
commute with each other. In fact, this commutation holds more generally for any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
as we now show.

Lemma 4.8
.

For any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, the labels of all
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
commute with each other and similarly the labels of all elements of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
commute.

Proof.

If
\mathsf{b}_{1},\mathsf{b}_{2}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
are two distinct elements, then they must be incomparable and both must be maximal elements of
\mathsf{w}_{1}
. To see this, note that if they were comparable, then at least one of them would not be maximal. If either was not maximal, then removing it from
\mathsf{w}_{1}
would not yield a valid order ideal.

Thus we can choose linear extensions of the partial order on
\mathsf{w}_{1}
where the final two elements are either
\mathsf{b}_{1}>\mathsf{b}_{2}
or
\mathsf{b}_{2}>\mathsf{b}_{1}
; clearly, since such total orders correspond to reduced expressions of
\Pi(\mathsf{w}_{1})
differing only in reversing the order of the final reflections
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{1})
and
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{2})
, this is only possible if
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{1})
and
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{2})
commute. The situation for
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
is identical.
∎

Second, we may also study the actions of moves between elements of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
in terms of their corresponding weights. Hence, we will in the following denote for a given order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
the corresponding weight by

\mu^{\vee}_{i}=\Pi(\mathsf{w}_{i})\cdot(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}}),

(4.2)

and we will similarly write
\mu^{\vee}_{i_{j}}=\Pi(\mathsf{w}_{i_{j}})\cdot(-{\varpi^{\vee}_{k}})
. We first establish two auxiliary statements which we will then use to characterize the possible moves in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
.

Lemma 4.9
.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, then for any
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
we have

\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle=0.

Proof.

The action of a simple reflection
s_{m}
on the weight
\mu^{\vee}_{i}
is given by
s_{m}(\mu^{\vee}_{i})=\mu^{\vee}_{i}-\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{i},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle\alpha^{\vee}_{m}
, and by minusculity we have
\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{i},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle\in\{-1,0,+1\}
. The three possibilities
\{-1,0,+1\}
correspond respectively to the situations: (1) there is some
\mathsf{b}
with label
s_{m}
such that
\mathsf{w}_{i}\sqcup\mathsf{b}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
is an order ideal, (2) no element with label
s_{m}
can be removed from or added to
\mathsf{w}_{i}
, and (3) there is some
\mathsf{b}
with label
s_{m}
such that
\mathsf{w}_{i}\setminus\mathsf{b}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
is an order ideal.

Now let
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
which is moved to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
. Then by above we compute that

\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle+\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle=1-1=0,

as claimed.
∎

Lemma 4.10
.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, then for any
m\in[n]
we have

\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{i_{1}}+\mu^{\vee}_{i_{2}},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{3}}}-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle.

Proof.

Since
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
is connected by moves, we may reduce the statement to establishing that

\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{3}+\mu^{\vee}_{4},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle

for
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
which can be obtained from
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
by a move
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. The first equality
\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{l}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{i_{1}}+\mu^{\vee}_{i_{2}},\alpha_{l}\rangle\!\rangle
will then follow by a straightforward induction on the number of moves between
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
and
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
. We now compute

\displaystyle\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{3}+\mu^{\vee}_{4},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle

\displaystyle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}-\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle\alpha^{\vee}_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}+\mu^{\vee}_{2}-\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle\alpha^{\vee}_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle

\displaystyle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle-\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})}\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle\alpha^{\vee}_{\mathrm{index}(\mathsf{b})},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle,

where the last equality follows from Lemma
4.9
. Proposition
3.7
now immediately implies the remainder of the lemma.
∎

Using these lemmas, we give a characterization of moves in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
.

Lemma 4.11
.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
, then
\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=-\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle
for any
m\in[n]\setminus\{i_{1},i_{3}\}
.

Proof.

By Lemma
4.10
, we have that

\langle\!\langle\mu^{\vee}_{1}+\mu^{\vee}_{2},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle=\langle\!\langle{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{3}}}-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}},\alpha_{m}\rangle\!\rangle.

Since
m\notin\{i_{1},i_{3}\}
, the right hand side is zero, and we immediately obtain the claim.
∎

For any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, we interpret the previous lemma as follows. For any maximal element
\mathsf{b}\in\mathsf{w}_{1}
which has label distinct from
s_{i_{1}},s_{i_{3}}
, if
\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}\neq\varnothing
, then
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. Similarly, for any maximal element
\mathsf{b}
of
\mathsf{w}_{2}
which has label distinct from
s_{i_{1}},s_{i_{3}}
, then
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
. The last statement follows from the fact that the unique maximal element of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
has label
s_{i_{3}}
and that every other element of
\mathsf{w}_{2}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
was moved from
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
. We now use moves between order ideals to distinguish embeddings of order ideals.

Definition 4.12
.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. For
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
which is moved to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{1}
, we define

\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\Bigl\{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})~\Big|~\tau_{i}:\mathsf{w}_{i}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P},~\text{$\tau_{1}^{\prime}|_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}=\tau_{1}$ and $\tau_{1}^{\prime}(\mathsf{b}^{\prime})=\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b})$ gives valid $\tau_{1}^{\prime}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}$}\Bigr\}.

Analogously for
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
which is moved to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
, we define

\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\Bigl\{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})~\Big|~\tau_{i}:\mathsf{w}_{i}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P},~\text{$\tau_{2}^{\prime}|_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\tau_{2}$ and $\tau_{2}^{\prime}(\mathsf{b}^{\prime})=\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b})$ gives valid $\tau_{2}^{\prime}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}$}\Bigr\}.

In the context of embeddings of order ideals, or equivalently terms of the toric expression of a Plücker monomial
p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}
, the set
\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
can be thought of as those toric pairs
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
which allow the removal of an element
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b})
from the image of
\tau_{2}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
and simultaneously the addition of the same element
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b})
to the image of
\tau_{1}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
. The set
\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
can be thought of similarly, but with the movement in the other direction from
\tau_{1}
to
\tau_{2}
. We will use
\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
to refine the information of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
in the sense that moves which may be allowed in general for order ideals
\mathsf{w}_{1}
and
\mathsf{w}_{2}
may not be allowed for particular embeddings
\tau_{1}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
and
\tau_{2}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
.

Example 4.13

(Continuing from Example
4.4
)
.

Consider again
\mathrm{LG}(5,10)=D_{5}^{\mathrm{sc}}/P_{5}
with
w^{P}
and
\mathsf{w}^{P}
given in (
4.1
). Then the order ideals

\left(\mathsf{w}_{1}=\raisebox{-14.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox Clearly we have
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b})\cap\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}(\mathsf{w}_{2})\neq\varnothing
, so the map from
\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
to
\mathsf{w}^{P}
sending
\mathsf{w}_{2}
to
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}(\mathsf{w}_{2})\subset\mathsf{w}^{P}
and
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
to
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b})
is
not
an embedding. On the other hand,
\tau_{2}
and
\tau_{3}
both map
\mathsf{b}
to the complement of
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
, so we do get valid embeddings of
\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
by extending
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}
to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
by
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b})
or
\tau_{3}(\mathsf{b})
. Hence, we find that

\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\bigl\{(\tau_{2},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}),~(\tau_{3},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{2}})\bigr\}

Now, consider the resulting pair of order ideals
\mathsf{w}_{3}=\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b}
and
\mathsf{w}_{4}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
. These order ideals of course allow the element
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
with label
s_{5}
to move back from
\mathsf{w}_{4}
to
\mathsf{w}_{3}
, and we indeed find
M_{\mathsf{w}_{4},\mathsf{w}_{3}}=\{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\}
. The ideal
\mathsf{w}_{3}
now consists of the leftmost two columns of
\mathsf{w}^{P}
, and hence has a single embedding, namely

\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}:\quad\mathsf{w}_{3}=\raisebox{-14.0pt}{\scriptsize\hskip 0.0pt{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt\hbox to6.4pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=5.12001pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.27997pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}=\mathsf{w}^{P}.

Note that
\tau_{4}(\mathsf{b}^{\prime})
and
\tau_{5}(\mathsf{b}^{\prime})
both lie in the complement of
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}(\mathsf{w}_{3})
, so the identity embedding on
\mathsf{w}_{3}
can be extended to
\mathsf{w}_{3}\sqcup\mathsf{b}
by defining the image of
\mathsf{b}
to be either of these elements. Hence, we find

\textup{I}^{s_{5}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}=\bigl\{(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{3}},\tau_{4}),~(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{3}},\tau_{5})\bigr\}.

Observe that the sets of embeddings
\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}^{\prime}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}
are closely related: if we consider the associated toric terms in the sense of (
2.10
), we find that the pairs of embeddings in
\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}^{\prime}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}
satisfy

a_{\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{1})}a_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}=a_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}a_{\tau_{4}(\mathsf{w}_{4})}\quad\text{and}\quad a_{\tau_{3}(\mathsf{w}_{1})}a_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}=a_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}a_{\tau_{5}(\mathsf{w}_{4})}

since
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{1})\cup\mathsf{w}_{2}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\cup\tau_{4}(\mathsf{w}_{4})
as well as
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{1})\cap\mathsf{w}_{2}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\cap\tau_{4}(\mathsf{w}_{4})
and analogously for the other toric expression. Hence, the corresponding terms in the toric expression for the Plücker coordinate expression
p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}-p_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{4}}
will cancel by (
2.13
).

\lozenge

In the discussion at the end of the above example we showed that there will be a natural correspondence of toric terms in a Plücker coordinate expression obtained by moving order ideal elements, and we will address the general situation in Lemma
4.23
. Before we handle the general situation, we have to be more precise with comparing the various toric terms, leading us to the following refinment of the partitioning of the toric terms for any
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
.

Definition 4.14
.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, then for any
A_{1}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
and
A_{2}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
we define the set of pairs of embeddings

T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\left(\bigcap_{\mathsf{b}\in A_{1}}\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\right)\cap\left(\bigcap_{\mathsf{b}\in A_{2}}\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\right)\cap\left(\bigcap_{\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\setminus A_{1}}(\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}})^{c}\right)\cap\left(\bigcap_{\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\setminus A_{2}}(\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}})^{c}\right),

where the complements in the definition above are taken with respect to the overall set of pairs of embeddings
\{(\tau_{1}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P},\tau_{2}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P})\}
. If a set
A_{i}=\{\mathsf{b}\}
consists of a single element, we will frequently abuse notation and simply write
\mathsf{b}
instead of
\{\mathsf{b}\}
.

Informally speaking, membership of a pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
in
T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
indicates that the images of
\tau_{1}
and
\tau_{2}
allow moves in
A_{2}
from
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{w}_{1})
to
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
as well as moves in
A_{1}
from
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
to
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{w}_{1})
, but do not allow moves in
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\setminus A_{1}
or in
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\setminus A_{2}
.
Note that any elements
\mathsf{B}\in(M_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\cup M_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}})\setminus(A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\cup A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}})
, do not play a role in the definition above. The reason for this is that if a move is not admissible, and hence does not occur between elements of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, it will not affect our cancellation argument in a meaningful way. Furthermore by construction, the sets
T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
T^{A_{1}^{\prime},A_{2}^{\prime}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
for
A_{1}\neq A_{1}^{\prime}
or
A_{2}\neq A_{2}^{\prime}
are disjoint. Thus for
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, these
T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
partition the toric terms of
p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}
via the decomposition

p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\sum_{(A_{1},A_{2})}\sum_{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})}a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}

where the first sum is over all pairs
(A_{1},A_{2})
with
A_{1}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
and
A_{2}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and the second sum is over all pairs
(\tau_{1},\tau_{1})\in T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. We now study this decomposition explicitly for the Plücker monomial
p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}
which corresponds to the top element
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
.

Lemma 4.15
.

The only nonempty toric sets for the top element
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
are

T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\bigl\{(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})\bigr\}\quad\text{and}\quad T^{\varnothing,\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}},

where
\mathsf{b}
is the maximal element of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
with label
s_{i_{2}}
, and these sets exhaust all toric terms of
p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}
.

Proof.

Recall from Proposition
3.7
that the weights corresponding to
p_{i_{1}}
and
p_{i_{2}}
are
{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{2}}}-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{1}}}
and
{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{3}}}-{\varpi^{\vee}_{i_{2}}}
. Thus
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
has a unique maximal element
\mathsf{b}
and this element has label
s_{i_{2}}
, and by Lemma
4.11
we have
A_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\{\mathsf{b}\}
which is moved to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
. Thus, any embedding
\tau_{i_{1}}:\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\rightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
has the unique maximal element
\tau_{i_{1}}(\mathsf{b})
. By Lemma
4.1
, the unique embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
in
\mathsf{w}^{P}
is the identity. Since no element of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
is labeled by
s_{i_{2}}
, the identity embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
in
\mathsf{w}^{P}
is the only embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
with image contained in
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
, and every other embedding
\tau_{i_{1}}:\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
must have its maximal element
\tau_{i_{1}}(\mathsf{b})\notin\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
.

For the identity embeddings
(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})
, since
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}(\mathsf{b})\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
, extending the identity embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
to
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
mapping it to
\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}(\mathsf{b})
is not a valid embedding of the order ideal
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
, so
(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})\notin\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}
. Next, for any other pair of embeddings
(\tau_{i_{1}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})
with
\tau_{i_{1}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}
, we have
\tau_{i_{1}}(\mathsf{b})\notin\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
, so mapping
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
to
\tau_{i_{1}}(\mathsf{b})
is in fact a valid extension of the identity embedding of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
to
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
, and thus
(\tau_{i_{1}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})\in\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}
for any non-identity embedding
\tau_{i_{1}}
of
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
. Thus, we have

\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\bigl\{(\tau,\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})~\big|~\tau\neq\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}\bigr\}\quad\text{and}\quad\Bigl(\textup{II}^{s_{i_{2}}}_{w_{i_{1}},w_{i_{2}}}\Bigr)^{c}=\bigl\{(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})\bigr\}.

Recall that
A_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\{\mathsf{b}\}
and
A_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}}=\varnothing
since
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
is the top element of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. In the case
A_{1}=A_{2}=\varnothing
, the only nontrivial set defining
T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}
is

T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\Bigl(\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}\Bigr)^{c}=\bigl\{(\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}},\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}})\bigr\}.

Next, in the case
A_{1}=\varnothing
and
A_{2}=\{\mathsf{b}\}
, the only nontrivial set defining
T^{\varnothing,\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}
is

T^{\varnothing,\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}=\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}.

Since these two sets exhaust all the toric terms of
p_{i_{1}}p_{i_{2}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
, and the toric sets are disjoint, the lemma follows.
∎

While the maximal element of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
is remarkable since
T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}}\neq\varnothing
, the other toric sets
T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
are empty, as we now show.

Lemma 4.16
.

For
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\neq(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, the toric set
T^{\varnothing,\varnothing}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
is empty.

Lemma
4.16
says that every pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
of the order ideals
\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}^{P}
allows some nonempty subset of the admissible moves
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\cup A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
between
\mathsf{w}_{1}
and
\mathsf{w}_{2}
.

Proof.

To prove the lemma, it is equivalent to show that for each
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
unequal to
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
and each pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P},\tau_{2}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P})
, at least one of the two sets
A_{1}=\{\mathsf{b}\mid(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\}
and
A_{2}=\{\mathsf{b}\mid(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\}
is nonempty. Note that all
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
unequal to
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
satisfy
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}\neq\varnothing
. Moreover, since
A_{1}\neq\varnothing
would satisfy the desired statement, we will establish this by considering the case where
A_{1}=\varnothing
and constructing an element of
A_{2}
.

We will first make a careful selection of an element of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
as follows. Since
\mathsf{w}_{2}\neq\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
, there must be a maximal element of
\mathsf{w}_{2}
with label unequal to
s_{i_{3}}
. Moreover, since
\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
has no element with label
s_{i_{3}}
by construction and the unique maximal element
\mathsf{b}_{\max}\in\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
has label
s_{i_{3}}
, we must also have
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{\max})=\mathsf{b}_{\max}
. Hence, any maximal element of
\mathsf{w}_{2}
can never become smaller in
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
than an element with label
s_{i_{3}}
. Since maximal elements of
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
are images of maximal elements of
\mathsf{w}_{2}
, there must thus be an element
\mathsf{b}_{2}\in\mathsf{w}_{2}
with
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{2})\neq s_{i_{3}}
that is maximal in
\mathsf{w}_{2}
and whose image
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2})\in\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
maximal as well. By Lemma
4.11
and the discussion following it, we have
\mathsf{b}_{2}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
. We fix such an element
\mathsf{b}_{2}\in\mathsf{w}_{2}
which moves to
\mathsf{b}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{1}
for the remainder of this proof.

Since
\mathsf{b}_{2}\notin A_{1}=\varnothing
, extending
\tau_{1}:\mathsf{w}_{1}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
to
\mathsf{w}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{2}^{\prime}
by mapping
\mathsf{b}_{2}^{\prime}
to
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2})
does
not
yield a valid embedding. This means that there must be a maximal element
\mathsf{b}_{1}\in\mathsf{w}_{1}
, whose label we write as
s_{m}=\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b}_{1})
, such that
\mathsf{b}_{1}<\mathsf{b}_{2}^{\prime}
and
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})>\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2})
. We will now show that
\mathsf{b}_{1}
is an element of
A_{2}
.

First, since
s_{m}
is the label of an element of
\mathsf{w}_{1}\vartriangleleft\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
, we have
s_{m}\neq s_{i_{1}}
. Furthermore, we have
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
since
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})>\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2})\geq\mathsf{b}_{2}
is larger than a maximal element of
\mathsf{w}_{2}
, so
s_{m}\neq s_{i_{3}}
as well. Lemma
4.11
then implies that
\mathsf{b}_{1}
is a move in
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
which moves to
\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
.

Finally, we show that extending
\tau_{2}:\mathsf{w}_{2}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
to
\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}
by mapping
\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}
to
\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})
is a valid embedding. If it is not, then there must be some
\mathsf{b}_{3}\in\mathsf{w}_{2}
such that
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{3})>\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})
. However, this yields the chain of inequalities

\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{3})>\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})>\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2}),

contradicting the maximality of
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{2})
in
\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})
. Thus we have
\mathsf{b}_{1}\in A_{2}
.
∎

Now that we have constructed and studied a way to classify embeddings of
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, we will need one final definition to organize the cancellation.

Definition 4.17
.

For a subset
\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
, we define the partial order that
a>b
in
\mathsf{C}
if and only if there exists a sequence
(a=c_{0},c_{1},\dots,b=c_{n})
of elements of
\mathsf{C}
such that for each
i
,
c_{i}\gtrdot c_{i+1}
is a cover relation in
\mathsf{P}
. We call
\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
an
m
-cube
if
\mathsf{C}
equipped with this partial order is isomorphic to the finite boolean lattice of subsets of an
m
-element set.

The reason for this terminology is that an
m
-cube in
\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
can be visualized in the Hasse diagram of
\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
as the
1
-skeleton (vertices and edges) of the
m
-cube
[0,1]^{m}
.

Remark 4.18
.

Note that the above definition does not use the natural induced poset structure on
\mathsf{C}
as a subset of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. For example, if
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
were the poset
a>b>c
, the natural induced partial order on
\{a,c\}
would be
a>c
while the partial order described above on
\{a,c\}
would be the two element antichain with
a
and
c
incomparable.

As a result, the poset
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
may generally allow many embeddings of boolean lattices which we do not call
m
-cubes by the definition above. For example, we have two order embeddings of the Boolean lattice in the following five element poset (drawn as Hasse diagrams with the largest element on the left where the filled-in circles are the image of the Boolean lattice), however the partial order on these subsets as given in Definition
4.17
yields the two posets on the right which are clearly not isomorphic to the Boolean lattice:

Hence, the two subposets are not
2
-cubes as defined in Definition
4.17
. One way to think of the partial order on
\mathsf{C}
is that it is the one whose Hasse diagram is obtained by removing vertices and edges from the Hasse diagram of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
if the vertex is not in
\mathsf{C}
or the edge has an endpoint not in
\mathsf{C}
.

These cubes will be the main tool for organizing our cancellation argument. Recall that every cover relation in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
corresponds to an admissible move between two elements of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, which we may also consider as a simple reflection via its label. Since cover relations of a cube
\mathsf{C}
are cover relations in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, we also obtain the same correspondence between cover relations in
\mathsf{C}
and labels describing admissible moves between elements of
\mathsf{C}
. Thus, we may associate to each cube
\mathsf{C}
the set
S_{\mathsf{C}}
of all labels corresponding to all cover relations between elements in
\mathsf{C}
. We next establish some elementary facts about
S_{\mathsf{C}}
, which we will refer to as the
set of labels
of
\mathsf{C}
.

Lemma 4.19
.

Let
\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
be an
m
-cube and
S_{\mathsf{C}}
its set of labels. Then
|S_{\mathsf{C}}|=m
and all elements of
S_{\mathsf{C}}
commute with each other.

Proof.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}})
denote the top element of
\mathsf{C}
. We claim that

S_{\mathsf{C}}=\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\mid\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}},(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}.

The inclusion “
\supset
” is straightforward: if
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}}
and
(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}
, then
\mathsf{b}
corresponds to a cover relation of
\mathsf{C}
and hence
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in S_{\mathsf{C}}
by definition. For the reverse inclusion, we will first show that if there is a cover relation
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
in
\mathsf{C}
with corresponding admissible move
\mathsf{b}_{*}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
which moves to
\mathsf{b}_{*}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}^{P}\setminus\mathsf{w}_{2}
, then

\{\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\mid(\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}=\{\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}\mid(\mathsf{w}_{3}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}\cup\{\mathsf{b}_{*}\}.

First, let
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
with
(\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}
and
\mathsf{b}\neq\mathsf{b}_{*}
(if
\mathsf{b}=\mathsf{b}_{*}
then
\mathsf{b}_{*}\in\{\mathsf{b}_{*}\}
and the claim holds). Let
\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}=\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b}
and
\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
. Since the union and intersection of order ideals are also order ideals, both
\mathsf{w}_{5}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\cap\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}
and
\mathsf{w}_{6}=\mathsf{w}_{4}\cup\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}
are order ideals. By this construction,
\mathsf{w}_{5}
can be obtained from
\mathsf{w}_{3}
by removing
\mathsf{b}
and from
\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}
by removing
\mathsf{b}_{*}
, while
\mathsf{w}_{6}
can be obtained from
\mathsf{w}_{4}
by adding
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
and from
\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}
by adding
\mathsf{b}_{*}^{\prime}
, so in particular
(\mathsf{w}_{5},\mathsf{w}_{6})
is covered by both
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
and
(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime})
in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
and is the unique such element. Then by definition of a cube,
\mathsf{C}
must contain
(\mathsf{w}_{5},\mathsf{w}_{6})=(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\wedge(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime})
. Thus, we find
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}
corresponding to
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{5}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{6}=\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})
in
\mathsf{C}
.

Conversely, let
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}
with
(\mathsf{w}_{3}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}
and furthermore let
\mathsf{w}_{5}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\setminus\mathsf{b}=\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\{\mathsf{b},\mathsf{b}_{*}\}
and
\mathsf{w}_{6}=\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\{\mathsf{b}^{\prime},\mathsf{b}_{*}^{\prime}\}
so
(\mathsf{w}_{5},\mathsf{w}_{6})\in\mathsf{C}
. Since
\mathsf{C}
is a cube, and we have the chain
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{5},\mathsf{w}_{6})
, there must be another element
(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}
such that
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{5},\mathsf{w}_{6})
where
(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime})
and
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
are incomparable. This implies that
\mathsf{w}_{1}\supset\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}\supset\mathsf{w}_{5}
and
\mathsf{w}_{2}\subset\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}\subset\mathsf{w}_{6}
. By construction,
\mathsf{w}_{5}
is obtained from
\mathsf{w}_{1}
by removing two elements
\mathsf{b},\mathsf{b}_{*}
. Since
\mathsf{w}_{3}
is obtained by removing
\mathsf{b}_{*}
from
\mathsf{w}_{1}
, the only possibility for
\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}
is that it must be obtained by removing
\mathsf{b}
from
\mathsf{w}_{1}
. Similarly, since
\mathsf{w}_{6}
is obtained from
\mathsf{w}_{2}
by adding
\mathsf{b}^{\prime},\mathsf{b}_{*}^{\prime}
and
\mathsf{w}_{4}
is obtained by adding
\mathsf{b}_{*}^{\prime}
to
\mathsf{w}_{2}
, the only possibility for
\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}
is that it must be obtained by adding
\mathsf{b}^{\prime}
to
\mathsf{w}_{2}
. Thus, we must have
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3}^{\prime}=\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{4}^{\prime}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})
in
\mathsf{C}
with corresponding move
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
.

With this result, we can now establish
S_{\mathsf{C}}\subset\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\mid\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}}\mid(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}
. Let
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in S_{\mathsf{C}}
, so that there is a cover relation
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\in\mathsf{C}
with corresponding move
\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. Since
\mathsf{C}
is a cube, there must also be a chain
(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}})\gtrdot\dots\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
in
\mathsf{C}
. Applying the previously established equality for each of these inclusions, we immediately conclude that
\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}}\mid(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}
. Since
\mathsf{C}
is an
m
-cube, it contains exactly
m
cover relations of the form
(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
so that the set
\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}}\mid(\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}}\setminus\mathsf{b},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}\sqcup\mathsf{b}^{\prime})\in\mathsf{C}\}
must correspondingly have exactly
m
elements. Finally, recall by Lemma
4.8
that the labels of elements of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{t_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{t_{2}}}
all commute when considered as Weyl group elements.
∎

Letting
\mathrm{label}(A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}})
denote the labels
\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\mid\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\}
corresponding to elements of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
, we obtain the following statement as an immediate corollary of the proof of Lemma
4.19
.

Corollary 4.20
.

Let
\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
be an
m
-cube and
S_{\mathsf{C}}
its set of labels. Then the map which sends
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}\mapsto\mathrm{label}(A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}})\cap S_{\mathsf{C}}
identifies
\mathsf{C}
with the Boolean lattice of subsets of
S_{\mathsf{C}}
. In particular, each element
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}
admits
m
moves with labels in
S_{\mathsf{C}}
, consisting of moves with labels in
\mathrm{label}(A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}})\cap S_{\mathsf{C}}
which go down in the partial order on
\mathsf{C}
and moves with labels in
\mathrm{label}(A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}})\cap S_{\mathsf{C}}
which go up in the partial order on
\mathsf{C}
.

Our definition of cube captures the situation where a pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
of the order ideals
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
is an element of
T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and the set consisting of all elements of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
obtainable from
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
using any moves with labels in
S=\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\mid\mathsf{b}\in A_{1}\cup A_{2}\}
forms an
|S|
-cube. We now show that this characterization is unique.

Lemma 4.21
.

If two
m
-cubes
\mathsf{C}_{1},\mathsf{C}_{2}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
have nonempty intersection and have the same set
S
of labels, then
\mathsf{C}_{1}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
.

Proof.

Let
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}_{1}\cap\mathsf{C}_{2}
. By Corollary
4.20
, for any subset
S^{\prime}\subset S
, the result of applying the moves with corresponding labels in
S^{\prime}
to
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
must be another element of
\mathsf{C}_{1}\cap\mathsf{C}_{2}
, which we denote by
S^{\prime}\cdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
. (Note that this element does not depend on the order of applying the moves due to the commutativity of the elements of
S
.) Furthermore, if
S_{1}^{\prime}\neq S_{2}^{\prime}
, then
S_{1}^{\prime}\cdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\neq S_{2}^{\prime}\cdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
. Thus, both
\mathsf{C}_{1}
and
\mathsf{C}_{2}
must contain the subset

\{S^{\prime}\cdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\mid S^{\prime}\subset S\}

which contains
2^{m}
elements. However, since any
m
-cube has exactly
2^{m}
elements, we must have that
\mathsf{C}_{1}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
are both equal to the set above.
∎

These are the main structural properties that we will need for
m
-cubes to organize our cancellation of toric terms. We now present our main technical result in this section about the uniformity of toric terms in an
m
-cube. To refer to pairs of embeddings yielding the same toric terms, we make the following definition:

Definition 4.22
.

Consider two elements
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}),(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\in\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
and corresponding embeddings
\tau_{i}:\mathsf{w}_{i}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{w}^{P}
. We say that
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
and
(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
are
torically equal
, written
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\overset{t}{=}(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
, if

a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}=a_{\tau_{3}}a_{\tau_{4}},

where we write
a_{\tau_{i}}=a_{\tau_{i}(\mathsf{w}_{i})}
, which is in turn defined in equation (
2.10
).

Note that the case that
a_{\tau_{1}}\neq a_{\tau_{3}}
or
a_{\tau_{2}}\neq a_{\tau_{4}}
is not excluded, as long as the products agree. To simplify notation in the remainder of this section, we will use
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}(S)
to denote the set
\{\mathsf{b}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\mid\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\in S\}
of moves in
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
whose labels are contained in the set of labels
S
.

Lemma 4.23
.

Let
\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{i_{*}}
be an
m
-cube with the set
S=S_{\mathsf{C}}
of labels. For any distinct pairs
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}),(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\in\mathsf{C}
, let
A_{12}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}(S)
,
A_{21}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S)
and similarly
A_{34}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}(S)
,
A_{43}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{4},\mathsf{w}_{3}}(S)
. There is a bijection

\kappa_{A_{21},A_{12}}^{A_{43},A_{34}}:T^{A_{21},A_{12}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}T^{A_{43},A_{34}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}

such that for any
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T^{A_{21},A_{12}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
, we have
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\overset{t}{=}\kappa_{A_{21},A_{12}}^{A_{43},A_{34}}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
.

Proof.

Since
\mathsf{C}
is connected by moves corresponding to labels in
S
, we may reduce to the case when
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
can be obtained from
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
by a single move with label in
S
. The full statement of the lemma then follows by a straightforward induction. Thus, we consider the two cases
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
and
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\lessdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
. To simplify notation, we will write
T_{12}=T^{A_{21},A_{12}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
T_{34}=T^{A_{43},A_{34}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}
, while writing
\kappa_{12}^{34}=\kappa_{A_{21},A_{12}}^{A_{43},A_{34}}
for the remainder of this proof.

In the first case,
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
corresponding to a move
\mathsf{b}_{3}\in A_{34}
which moves to
\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime}
, we have
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})=(\mathsf{w}_{3}\setminus\mathsf{b}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{2}=\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime})
. In this case, we define
\kappa_{12}^{34}
as follows. Given a pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T_{12}
of
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, we define the embeddings
(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
of
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
by setting

\tau_{3}|_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}=\tau_{1}\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{3}(\mathsf{b}_{3})=\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime}),\quad\text{while}\quad\tau_{4}=\tau_{2}|_{\mathsf{w}_{4}}.

We then set
\kappa_{12}^{34}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})=(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
. The fact that this defines a map
\kappa_{12}^{34}:T_{12}\rightarrow T_{34}
follows immediately from the definitions of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
and
\textup{I}^{\mathsf{b}_{3}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
along with Corollary
4.20
.

In the second case,
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\lessdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
corresponding to a move
\mathsf{b}_{1}\in A_{12}
which moves to
\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}
, we have
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})=(\mathsf{w}_{1}\setminus\mathsf{b}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{4}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime})
. In this case, we define
\kappa_{12}^{34}
as follows. Given a pair of embeddings
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T_{12}
of
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, we define the embeddings
(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
of
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})
by setting

\tau_{3}=\tau_{1}|_{\mathsf{w}_{3}},\quad\text{while}\quad\tau_{4}|_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}=\tau_{2}\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{4}(\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime})=\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1}).

We then set
\kappa_{12}^{34}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})=(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})
. Similarly to before, the fact that
\kappa_{12}^{34}
is well-defined follows immediately from the definitions of
A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
and
\textup{II}^{\mathsf{b}_{1}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
along with Corollary
4.20
.

We now show in both cases that
\kappa_{34}^{12}\circ\kappa_{12}^{34}=\mathrm{id}
. Fix any pair
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T_{12}
and write
(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})=\kappa_{12}^{34}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
and
(\tau_{1}^{\prime},\tau_{2}^{\prime})=\kappa_{34}^{12}\circ\kappa_{12}^{34}(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})
. First, suppose that
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, then

\tau_{1}^{\prime}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{3}|_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{1},\quad\text{while}\quad\tau_{2}^{\prime}|_{\mathsf{w}_{4}}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{4}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{2}|_{\mathsf{w}_{4}}\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{2}^{\prime}(\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime})\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{3}(\mathsf{b}_{3})\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime})

where
\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}_{2}
and
\mathsf{b}_{3}\in\mathsf{w}_{3}
are as above. In the second case,
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\lessdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, we instead find

\tau_{1}^{\prime}|_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{3}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{1}|_{\mathsf{w}_{3}}\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{1}^{\prime}(\mathsf{b}_{1})\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{4}(\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime})\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1}),\quad\text{while}\quad\tau_{2}^{\prime}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}\tau_{4}|_{\mathsf{w}_{4}}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}\tau_{2},

with
\mathsf{b}_{1}\in\mathsf{w}_{1}
and
\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathsf{w}_{4}
as above.

We now prove the toric equality in both cases. As before, let
(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T_{12}
, write
(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})=\kappa_{12}^{34}
, and consider the two cases. First, suppose
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, so
\mathsf{w}_{3}=\mathsf{w}_{1}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{3}
and
\mathsf{w}_{2}=\mathsf{w}_{4}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime}
as above, then

a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}=a_{\tau_{1}(\mathsf{w}_{1})}a_{\tau_{2}(\mathsf{b}_{3}^{\prime})}a_{\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{4})}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_1}}}{=\!=}a_{\tau_{3}(\mathsf{w}_{1})}a_{\tau_{3}(\mathsf{b}_{3})}a_{\tau_{4}(\mathsf{w}_{4})}=a_{\tau_{3}}a_{\tau_{4}}.

Second, suppose
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\lessdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
, so
\mathsf{w}_{1}=\mathsf{w}_{3}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{1}
and
\mathsf{w}_{4}=\mathsf{w}_{2}\sqcup\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime}
as above, then

a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}=a_{\tau_{1}(\mathsf{w}_{3})}a_{\tau_{1}(\mathsf{b}_{1})}a_{\tau_{2}(\mathsf{w}_{2})}\overset{\text{\eqref{aux_eq:def_kappa_case_2}}}{=\!=}a_{\tau_{3}(\mathsf{w}_{3})}a_{\tau_{4}(\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime})}a_{\tau_{4}(\mathsf{w}_{2})}=a_{\tau_{3}}a_{\tau_{4}}

completing the proof of the statement.
∎

We are finally ready to prove the main theorem of this section. For this, we define
L_{d}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
to be the set of pairs
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
which can be obtained from the top element
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
by a minimal length sequence of
d\geq 0
moves

\mathsf{b}_{1}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}},\quad\dots,\quad\mathsf{b}_{d}\in A_{\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}\setminus\{\mathsf{b}_{1},\dots,\mathsf{b}_{d-1}\},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}\sqcup\{\mathsf{b}_{1}^{\prime},\dots,\mathsf{b}_{d-1}^{\prime}\}}

from
\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}}
to
\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}}
. (Here, minimality is considered among all sequences of moves between
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
and
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
.) If there are no such pairs in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
, then we define
L_{d}=\varnothing
. In particular, since
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
is finite, then
L_{d}=\varnothing
for all
d
sufficiently large.

Theorem 4.24
.

The generalized minor
\phi_{{i_{*}}}
is equal on
U_{-}^{P}
to the polynomial
\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}
obtained as the alternating sum over the sets
L_{d}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}

\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}=\sum_{d\geq 0}(-1)^{d}\sum_{(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in L_{d}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}.

Proof.

We will prove this statement by computing the restrictions of both sides to the open, dense torus
U^{\circ}_{-}\subset U_{-}^{P}
and verifying that they are equal. The desired result then follows from the irreducibility of
U_{-}^{P}
. We computed the restriction
\phi_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
in Theorem
3.10
, so we now focus on the claimed Plücker coordinate expression. We begin by rewriting the restriction of the Plücker coordinate expression using the toric sets
T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}

\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\sum_{d\geq 0}(-1)^{d}\sum_{(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in L_{d}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{1}}p_{\mathsf{w}_{2}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\sum_{d\geq 0}(-1)^{d}\sum_{(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in L_{d}}\sum_{A_{1},A_{2}}\sum_{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}}a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}

where the third sum on the rightmost side is over all subsets
A_{1}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
and
A_{2}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. For each
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
and each pair
A_{1}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}
and
A_{2}\subset A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
, there is a unique
(|A_{1}|+|A_{2}|)
-cube with the set
\{\mathrm{label}(\mathsf{b})\mid\mathsf{b}\in A_{1}\cup A_{2}\}
of labels containing
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
by Lemma
4.21
.

For any cube
\mathsf{C}
, let
d_{\mathsf{C}}
denote the minimum number of moves in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
between the top element
(\mathsf{w}_{i_{1}},\mathsf{w}_{i_{2}})
of
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
and the top element of
\mathsf{C}
and let
S_{\mathsf{C}}
denote the set of labels of
\mathsf{C}
. Then we may rewrite the sum above by instead summing over all cubes contained in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
. Before rewriting it like this, we first note that by Lemma
4.23
, we have for all cubes
\mathsf{C}
and all pairs
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}),(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\in\mathsf{C}
that

\sum_{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T^{A_{1},A_{2}}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}}a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}=\sum_{(\tau_{3},\tau_{4})\in T^{A_{3},A_{4}}_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}}a_{\tau_{3}}a_{\tau_{4}},

where
A_{1}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}}),A_{2}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})
and
A_{3}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{4},\mathsf{w}_{3}}(S_{\mathsf{C}}),A_{4}=A_{\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})
. Thus the sum of monomials corresponding to pairs of embeddings in the toric set
T^{A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}}),A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
is independent of the particular element
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}
, so for each cube
\mathsf{C}
we will simply use
T_{\mathsf{C}}^{S_{\mathsf{C}}}
to denote any one of the torically equivalent toric sets
T^{A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}}),A_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})}_{\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2}}
. We now rewrite the sum as

\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}=\sum_{\mathsf{C}\subset\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}}\sum_{(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}}(-1)^{d_{\mathsf{C}}+|A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})|}\sum_{(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\in T_{\mathsf{C}}^{S_{\mathsf{C}}}}a_{\tau_{1}}a_{\tau_{2}}.

Furthermore, by Corollary
4.20
,
|A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})|
is equal to the number of cover relations of the form
(\mathsf{w}_{3},\mathsf{w}_{4})\gtrdot(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
in
\mathsf{C}
(i.e. where
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})
is the lesser element) and for a fixed
j
, there are
\binom{|S_{\mathsf{C}}|}{j}
elements
(\mathsf{w}_{1},\mathsf{w}_{2})\in\mathsf{C}
with
|A_{\mathsf{w}_{2},\mathsf{w}_{1}}(S_{\mathsf{C}})|=j
. Thus we may further rewrite the previous sum over all cubes in
\mathsf{P}_{{i_{*}}}
as

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{{i_{*}}}|_{U^{\circ}_{-}}
